objective_pt: Tell an anecdote vividly: mix narrative tenses (past perfect, past continuous), use precise verbs ("stumbled", "glanced") and build suspense ("It was only when... that...").

teacher.goal_pt: Elicit a short anecdote and listen for tense control and detail.
prompts: Tell me about a time something went completely wrong on a trip.
What had you expected to happen?
watchFor: Everything in the simple past, with no background (past continuous) or earlier events (past perfect).
"Then... then... then..." as the only linker.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat, slowing down slightly before the twist.
exercises.prompt: I'd been waiting for an hour when I realised I was at the wrong station.
accepted: I'd been waiting for an hour when I realised I was at the wrong station
I'd been waiting for an hour when I realized I was at the wrong station
I had been waiting for an hour when I realised I was at the wrong station

exercises.instruction_pt: Which sentence makes it clear that the film started before they arrived?
options: When we arrived, the film started.
When we arrived, the film had already started.
When we arrived, the film was starting.
exercises.explanation_pt: The past perfect ("had started") shows the earlier action. With the simple past, the film starts when they arrive.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Quando cheguei, todo mundo já tinha ido embora."
accepted: When I arrived, everyone had already left
When I got there, everyone had already left
When I arrived, everybody had already left
When I got there, everybody had already gone
When I arrived, everyone had already gone
By the time I arrived, everyone had already left
By the time I got there, everyone had left
By the time I got there, everyone had already gone home

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Everyone" is grammatically singular, but here the tense is the issue: use the past perfect, "everyone had already left".
commonErrors.correction_en: When I arrived, everyone had already left.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Já tinha ido" is an action before another past action, so the past perfect is clearer: "had already left".
commonErrors.correction_en: When I arrived, everyone had already left.

teacher.goal_pt: Replace generic verbs (go, look, say) with precise narrative verbs: stumble, glance, mutter, rush, stare.
prompts: Show me the difference between "glance" and "stare".
When did you last rush somewhere?
watchFor: "Realise" used for "perceber" correctly, but "notice" vs "realise" confused.

exercises.example_en: She glanced at her watch and frowned.
We stumbled across a tiny restaurant in the old town.
He muttered something about the weather and left.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each storytelling verb with its meaning.
Say this in natural English: "Foi aí que eu percebi que tinha esquecido o passaporte."
accepted: That's when I realised I'd forgotten my passport
That's when I realized I had forgotten my passport
That's when I realised I'd left my passport behind
It was then that I realised I'd forgotten my passport
That was when I realised I'd forgotten my passport
That's when it hit me that I'd forgotten my passport
That's when I noticed I'd forgotten my passport

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Perceber" (to become aware) is "realise", not "perceive", which is formal and about the senses.
commonErrors.correction_en: That's when I realised I'd forgotten my passport.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: English uses possessives with personal belongings: "my passport", not "the passport".
commonErrors.correction_en: That's when I realised I'd forgotten my passport.

teacher.goal_pt: Pacing and pausing for suspense; the three "-ed" endings in narrative verbs.
prompts: Say "And then... nothing." with a dramatic pause.
watchFor: Adding an extra syllable to "rushed" ("rush-ed") or "glanced" ("glan-ced").

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat. "Rushed" and "stopped" end in /t/, one syllable each.
exercises.prompt: I rushed to the door and stopped dead.
accepted: I rushed to the door and stopped dead

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat with a short pause after "door" to build suspense.
exercises.prompt: And there, standing at the door, was my old boss.
accepted: And there, standing at the door, was my old boss

exercises.instruction_pt: Which verb has an extra syllable in the past tense?
exercises.explanation_pt: Verbs ending in /t/ or /d/ add /ɪd/: wai-ted. "Glanced" (/t/) and "stumbled" (/d/) don't add a syllable.

teacher.goal_pt: Follow the order of events in a story told out of sequence and react naturally.
prompts: How would you react if a friend told you this?
watchFor: Assuming events happened in the order they were mentioned.
Reacting with just "OK" instead of showing interest.

exercises.listen: By the time the taxi turned up, I'd already missed the flight, and I'd been arguing with the airline for twenty minutes.
options: The speaker started arguing with the airline.
exercises.explanation_pt: Both past perfects are earlier than the taxi, and the argument came after missing the flight.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen to your friend and react with interest, asking what happened next.
exercises.listen: So I opened the door, and guess who was standing there?
accepted: Who?
No idea, who?
Who was it?
I have no idea. Who was it?
Go on, who was it?
Who was standing there?
Don't tell me it was your ex!
Who? Tell me!
I can't guess. Who?
Who was there?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: In a direct question, the verb comes before "there": "Who was there?".

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and say what you think had happened to the speaker's phone.
exercises.listen: I got home and the phone wasn't in my bag. It turned out I'd left it on the bus.
accepted: You'd left it on the bus
You had left it on the bus
You left it on the bus
It was on the bus
You left your phone on the bus
You'd left your phone on the bus
It had been left on the bus
It was still on the bus

commonErrors.explanation_pt: We say "on the bus" (also "on the train", "on the plane"), not "in the bus". And "esquecer em um lugar" is usually "leave".
commonErrors.correction_en: You'd left it on the bus.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: With buses, trains and planes, English uses "on": "on the bus".
commonErrors.correction_en: You'd left it on the bus.

teacher.goal_pt: Tell a 1–2 minute anecdote with setting, complication, climax and resolution.
prompts: Tell me about the most embarrassing moment of your life.
Where were you and what were you doing at the time?
How did it end? Would you do anything differently?

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Eu estava andando para casa quando começou a chover."
accepted: I was walking home when it started to rain
I was walking home when it started raining
I was walking home when it began to rain
I was walking home when it began raining
I was on my way home when it started to rain
I was walking back home when it started raining

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Home" works like an adverb after verbs of movement: "walk home", "go home", without "to".
commonErrors.correction_en: I was walking home when it started to rain.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: English needs a subject for weather: "it started to rain".
commonErrors.correction_en: I was walking home when it started to rain.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Só quando cheguei ao hotel é que percebi o erro."
accepted: It was only when I got to the hotel that I realised my mistake
It was only when I arrived at the hotel that I realised my mistake
It was only when I got to the hotel that I noticed the mistake
It wasn't until I got to the hotel that I realised my mistake
It wasn't until I arrived at the hotel that I realised the mistake
Only when I got to the hotel did I realise my mistake
Only when I arrived at the hotel did I realise my mistake
I only realised my mistake when I got to the hotel

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Chegar a" is "arrive at" (a building) or "arrive in" (a city), never "arrive to". Or say "get to".
commonErrors.correction_en: It was only when I got to the hotel that I realised my mistake.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: If you start with "Only when...", invert the main clause: "...did I realise". Or use "It was only when... that I realised".
commonErrors.correction_en: Only when I got to the hotel did I realise my mistake.

exercises.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to start a story.
accepted: You'll never guess what happened to me yesterday

exercises.instruction_pt: Tell the story in one or two minutes, with as much vivid detail as you can.
exercises.prompt_en: Tell me about a time when a small mistake led to something unexpected, good or bad. Set the scene first.
guidelines_pt: Set the scene with the past continuous: "I was sitting...".
Use the past perfect for what had happened before.
Use at least two precise verbs (glance, rush, stumble, mutter...).
Build up to the climax: "It was only when... that...", then say how it ended.

teacher.goal_pt: Check narrative tenses and prepositions of transport and arrival.
prompts: What were you doing at 8 pm yesterday?
What had you done before breakfast today?

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Ele parecia que não dormia havia dias."
accepted: He looked like he hadn't slept for days
He looked as if he hadn't slept for days
He looked as though he hadn't slept for days
He looked like he hadn't slept in days
He seemed like he hadn't slept for days
It looked like he hadn't slept for days
It looked as if he hadn't slept in days

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ele parecia que..." is "He looked like..." / "He looked as if...", not "He seemed that".
commonErrors.correction_en: He looked as if he hadn't slept for days.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: For a period up to a past moment, use the past perfect: "hadn't slept for days".
commonErrors.correction_en: He looked as if he hadn't slept for days.

exercises.sentence: We finally arrived ___ the airport at midnight.
accepted: at

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Use "arrive at" for a specific place (airport, station, hotel); "arrive in" for cities and countries.
commonErrors.correction_en: We finally arrived at the airport at midnight.

exercises.explanation_pt: "Glance" is a quick look. "Stare" and "gaze" are long looks.

exercises.prompt: Looking back, it was one of the best things that ever happened to me.
accepted: Looking back, it was one of the best things that ever happened to me
